claims.text: Header: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs'; effective September 12, 2024; reissues and cancels DoDI 5205.11, February 6, 2013, as amended; also incorporates and cancels the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum, 'Integrated Joint Special Technical Operations (IJSTO) Policy', April 5, 2021; approved by Kathleen H. Hicks, Deputy Secretary of Defense.

WHAT MAKES A PROGRAM WAIVED, in DoD's own words. Para 1.2.f.: 'The Secretary of Defense may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived" when it is determined that using standard procedures for reporting to Congress would adversely affect national security.' The waiver therefore attaches only to programs that are ALREADY unacknowledged; waived is a subset of unacknowledged, not a parallel category.

Glossary definitions verbatim: 'acknowledged SAP: A SAP whose existence is acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to others, but its specific details are classified.' 'unacknowledged SAP: A SAP having enhanced security measures, ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged.' 'waived SAP: A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable reporting following a determination of adverse effect to national security.'

WHO GETS TOLD. Para 7.2.a.(3): 'Only the chair, the ranking member, the staff directors, and one designated security manager of the defense and intelligence committees will be authorized access to waived DoD SAPs.' Para 7.2.b.: 'Members of Congress assigned to the defense and intelligence committees are authorized access to all DoD SAPs within the respective committee's SAP oversight jurisdiction, except for waived programs.'

Para 7.2.f. verbatim: 'The personal staff of a member of Congress will not be granted access to DoD SAPs.' Non-committee members and staff may be granted access only to NON-waived SAPs, and only 'by the Director, DoD SAPCO following consultation with the respective chamber' (7.2.d.). Senate and House leadership may each nominate one professional staff member for access to all DoD SAPs (7.2.e.).
BUDGET PAPER TRAIL. Para 7.2.h. (congressional budget justification materials): waived program justification material goes only to committee staff directors, not to the committees as bodies.

GAO ACCESS IS GATED. Para 7.2.g.: authorized access approval authorities may grant SAP access to GAO staff for specific projects only after the Director, DoD SAPCO consults with the chairman and ranking defense committee members. Congress's own audit arm cannot reach a DoD SAP without the audited department's SAPCO first clearing it with four members.

Para 7.1.: 'All DoD employees accessed to DoD SAPs will coordinate with and notify the DoD and OA SAPCOs through the CA SAPCO when intending to brief or provide DoD SAP material to any appropriately accessed members of Congress or professional staff member.' A cleared DoD employee cannot lawfully brief even an accessed member of Congress without first routing notice through the SAP's own control office.

PERIODIC REVIEW OF WAIVED STATUS EXISTS. Para 3.5.a.(3)(d) makes the SAPOC annual review cover 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status,' as part of the 3.5.a.(3) mandate to 'Conduct an annual review of DoD SAPs to assess the continuing need for protection of CPI within SAP security controls, in accordance with E.O. 13526 and DoDD 5205.07.'

TIER ARCHITECTURE. DoDI 5205.11 establishes a tiered SAP structure: umbrellas at tier 1, compartments at tier 2, sub-compartments at tier 3 and below; only the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense may alter tier 1 structures. It distinguishes 'structural SAP: A SAP that provides organization to the architecture and does not protect discrete CPI' from 'content SAP: A SAP that protects discrete CPI.'

The structural/content distinction is load-bearing for any search of SAP nomenclature: a structural SAP is a container with a codeword and no content of its own, so a program name appearing in budget or security documentation may correspond to no discrete body of protected information at all. Conversely, discrete CPI can be moved between compartments under an unchanged tier-1 umbrella name without any tier-1 action reaching the Secretary. Reasoning stated from the 1.2 tier description.

Para 4.1.a.(2): 'Within 45 calendar days of creation of the SAP project, the CA will submit' the required documentation — establishing an internal 45-day paper deadline for new SAP projects, distinct from the statutory 30-day congressional pre-initiation notice under 10 U.S.C. 119(f).

Para 5.1.e.(1): 'The use of a polygraph examination as a mandatory access determination requirement must be approved by the Secretary of Defense.' Mandatory-polygraph SAP access is a Secretary-level decision, which makes the presence of a polygraph requirement a marker of a program that reached the top of the department.

DoDI 5205.11 Appendix 3 to Enclosure 6, sample action memo to the Deputy Secretary of Defense: 'The Defense Security Service will be carved out from its normal industrial security oversight responsibilities.'

DoDI 5205.11 sample action memo recommendation: 'That you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize carve-out status and the mandatory administration of CI polygraphs, and that you sign the notification letters to Congress (TAB C) identifying GREEN TREE as a new SAP.'

DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 7 requires each SAP record file to include 'Written approval by SecDef or DepSecDef of carve-out status when DSS is relieved of industrial security oversight responsibilities' and 'The identification of SAP facilities (or identification of the SAPCO-approved database that contains the information) that have been carved-out based upon this authority.'

DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 6 PSAP timeline: 'NLT P+180 - DepSecDef decision. Congressional notification or PSAP termination as appropriate. NLT P+210 - End of 30-day period without Congressional decision.'

DoDI 5205.11 SAP Approval Package Checklist item 2: 'Type, Category, and Classification of SAP. If unacknowledged and reporting requirements are to be waived, attach justification to waive the requirements of Volumes 2A and 2B of DoD 7000.14-R.'

DoDI 5205.11 Glossary: 'waived SAP. A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting in accordance with Reference (c) following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.'

DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d requires every DoD SAP to be assigned an unclassified nickname generated under CJCSM 3150.29D, and provides that 'Unclassified nicknames will be used in the annual SAP report to Congress.'

DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 2 requires the Director, DoD SAPCO to establish 'policies and applicable procedures to satisfy reporting requirements for DSS carve-outs' and to provide 'DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions.'

Because the annual SAP report to Congress uses only unclassified nicknames, a member reading the list sees a word, not a mission. Reasoning: DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d expressly directs nickname use in the annual report and leaves the codeword optional and classified.

connections.note: The statute permits the waiver; this Instruction is where the Department operates it. Para 1.2.f. is DoD's own designation authority - the Secretary 'may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived"' - and Enclosure 3 tasks the Senior Review Group with reviewing 'all waived DoD SAPs' annually and advising the SAPOC. Para 7.2.a.(3) then sets who is told, and it is wider than the statute's twelve: the chair, the ranking member, the staff directors and one designated security manager of the defense AND intelligence committees. Quotations are the verbatim ones already recorded on this node from the Instruction itself.

desc: DoDI 5205.11 is the single most useful public document on this board, because it does not merely define the mechanism - it walks through it, with a worked example and a timeline. Enclosure 6 sets out the prospective SAP (PSAP) approval sequence in days from establishment: SSWG review by P+14, draft security classification guide by P+45, approval package to the Senior Review Group by P+90, SRG convenes at P+105, final package to the SAPOC at P+130, SAPOC convenes at P+150, Deputy Secretary of Defense decision and congressional notification or termination at P+180, and 'End of 30-day period without Congressional decision' at P+210. The last line is the statutory clock of 10 U.S.C. 119(f) reduced to a checkbox: Congress is not asked to approve anything, it is notified, and after thirty days of silence the program starts. Appendix 2 to Enclosure 6 is the SAP Approval Package Checklist, whose item 2 requires that 'If unacknowledged and reporting requirements are to be waived, attach justification to waive the requirements of Volumes 2A and 2B of DoD 7000.14-R' - the Financial Management Regulation - and whose item 11.d requires a 'Contract strategy (carve-out justification if applicable)'. Appendix 3 is an unclassified sample Action Memo to the Deputy Secretary of Defense recommending establishment of a fictional unacknowledged operations and support SAP nicknamed GREEN TREE, in which the Director of DoD SAPCO writes: 'The Defense Security Service will be carved out from its normal industrial security oversight responsibilities' and recommends 'that you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize carve-out status and the mandatory administration of CI polygraphs'. Enclosure 7 then requires that each SAP record file contain 'Written approval by SecDef or DepSecDef of carve-out status when DSS is relieved of industrial security oversight responsibilities' and 'The identification of SAP facilities ... that have been carved-out based upon this authority'. Those two records are the FOIA target that would settle the question of how many carved-out facilities exist.

claims.text: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs (SAPs),' is effective February 6, 2013, is signed by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, cancels the classified DoDI 0-5205.11 of July 1, 1997, and carries releasability 'Unlimited.'

The Instruction defines an unacknowledged SAP as 'A SAP having enhanced security measures ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized for such information.'

The Instruction defines a waived SAP as 'A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting ... following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.'

The SAP governance structure consists of the SAP Oversight Committee (SAPOC), the Senior Review Group (SRG) and the SAP Senior Working Group (SSWG), which 'advise and assist the SecDef and DepSecDef in the management, administration, and oversight of DoD SAPs'; the SRG 'Reviews all waived DoD SAPs annually' and recommends to the SAPOC on continued waived status.

The Instruction provides that a SAP 'may not be initiated until the congressional defense committees are notified of the program and a period of 30 days has elapsed after such notification is received,' and that upon approval 'the DepSecDef will submit formal notification letters to Congress that the SAP has been established.'

The Instruction sets the congressional reporting calendar as SAP Listing due February 1 and SAP Annual Report due March 1, forwarded to the congressional defense committees by the DoD SAPCO, and states that the SAP report 'is submitted to Congress in accordance with section 119 of Title 10, United States Code.'

claims.source: Statutory note, 'Termination of Reporting Requirements,' 10 U.S.C. 119, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title10/html/USCODE-2023-title10-subtitleA-partI-chap2-sec119.htm
claims.text: The statutory obligations behind that calendar -- the annual SAP report at 10 U.S.C. 119(a) and the new-SAP notice and justification at 10 U.S.C. 119(b) -- were terminated effective December 31, 2021 by section 1061 of Public Law 114-328.

The Instruction establishes a four-level hierarchy -- umbrella, compartment, sub-compartment, project -- in which a person accessed to a compartment is also accessed to all subordinate elements unless the CA SAPCO approves an exception, subordinate elements are presumed to be of the same type as the parent, and unacknowledged waived sub-elements added under a non-waived umbrella are expressly addressed as a distinct case requiring SAPCO action.

Cognizant Authority SAPCOs must notify the Director, DoD SAPCO in writing of proposals for change of category; 'Change of type (acknowledged, unacknowledged)'; 'Alteration of scope'; IJSTO apportionment or deapportionment; disestablishment (termination, cancellation, transition); 'Support of non-DoD SAPs'; addition, deletion or changes of compartments, sub-compartments and projects; 'Proposals to relieve DSS of NISP security oversight responsibilities (carve-out) when required'; 'Change of nickname, codeword, PID'; and 'Foreign involvement.'

Access is conditioned on a determination that the individual 'has a valid NTK, has the requisite security clearance, meets approved personnel prerequisites, and will clearly and materially contribute to the execution or oversight of the program' -- a discretionary gate held by the programme.

Whenever a SAP's classification is to change or SAP information is to be declassified and made public, the DoD SAPCO must give the congressional defense committees a report describing the proposed changes, the reasons, and notice of any planned public announcement.

claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Enclosure 6 appendices (sample SAP approval memorandum), https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf
claims.text: Sample SAP approval documentation reproduced in the Instruction uses a notional unacknowledged operations-and-support SAP designated GTE with planned unacknowledged sub-compartments including LEAF BARK (LBK), and a recommendation line reading 'That you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize.'

A SAP disestablishment plan must address contracting, fiscal, audit, property disposition, classified material disposition, training, public affairs, legal, logistics and technical actions, and the CA SAPCO must provide the termination plan to the DoD SAPCO for SSWG review of potential impact on other programs.

The Instruction contains a self-expiry clause: it 'Must be reissued, cancelled, or certified current within 5 years of its publication in accordance with DoDI 5025.01. If not it will expire effective February 6, 2023 and be removed from the DoD Issuances Website.'

connections: Implements 10 U.S.C. 119, the statute whose subsection (e) waiver and December 31, 2021 reporting termination are the core of classified-annex.
The 'will clearly and materially contribute to the execution or oversight of the program' access gate is the doctrinal basis for the read-on denial David Grusch testified to on July 26, 2023.

'Support of non-DoD SAPs' is the doctrinal bridge to the DHS compartment KONA BLUE would have become, and to the IC Controlled Access Program AARO says was expanded in 2021 to protect UAP reverse-engineering.

The carve-out provision relieving the Defense Security Service of National Industrial Security Program oversight is the mechanism by which contractor facilities performing SAP work fall outside routine DoD industrial security inspection.
'Change of nickname, codeword, PID' is the doctrinal answer to why a legacy effort would be untrackable across decades even to cleared reviewers.
The February 1 SAP Listing and March 1 SAP Annual Report are the documents that, if they still existed, would settle whether an unreported UAP materials programme is inside the DoD SAP inventory.
Deputy Secretary of Defense signature authority makes the DepSecDef, not the SecDef, the approving official for SAP establishment -- a specific office to interrogate for any given programme's origin.
dossier.denialPosture: None. DoDI 5205.11 asserts nothing about UAP and denies nothing; it is a procedural issuance published with unlimited releasability. Its evidentiary value is that the Department has openly documented, in its own doctrine, every structural capability -- unacknowledged type, waived reporting, nested waived sub-elements under reported umbrellas, industrial-security carve-outs, and discretionary denial of oversight read-ons -- that a concealed legacy programme would require.
dossier.narrative:
The most useful thing about DoDI 5205.11 is that it is unclassified and approved for public release with unlimited releasability. The Department published its own concealment architecture and nobody read it.

Start with the vocabulary, because the Glossary is where the load is carried. An 'unacknowledged SAP' is 'A SAP having enhanced security measures ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized for such information.' A 'waived SAP' is 'A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting ... following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.' A 'waiver' more generally is 'A decision that provides an approved exception to or deviation from a SAP security standard.' Two of the three definitions describe subtraction from the oversight baseline.

The waiver traces to statute. 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) lets the Secretary of Defense waive any requirement that certain information be included in a SAP report where inclusion 'would adversely affect the national security,' case by case; 119(e)(2) routes the withheld content and the justification 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees.' Twelve members. No staff named. That is the entire congressional footprint of a waived SAP.

The governance layer is three committees stacked above the Deputy Secretary: the SAP Oversight Committee (SAPOC), the Senior Review Group (SRG), and the SAP Senior Working Group (SSWG), which 'advise and assist the SecDef and DepSecDef in the management, administration, and oversight of DoD SAPs.' The SRG 'Reviews all waived DoD SAPs annually' and provides recommendations to the SAPOC 'concerning continued waived status.' There is, in other words, an internal annual re-authorisation cycle for programmes Congress cannot see -- run entirely by the Department.

Establishment is the part that looks like oversight. The SAPOC reviews the package and submits it to the Deputy Secretary of Defense for decision. 'If approved, the DepSecDef will submit formal notification letters to Congress that the SAP has been established.' And: 'The SAP may not be initiated until the congressional defense committees are notified of the program and a period of 30 days has elapsed after such notification is received.' That mirrors 10 U.S.C. 119(f). The Instruction also fixes the annual reporting calendar: SAP Listing on February 1, SAP Annual Report on March 1, forwarded to the congressional defense committees by the DoD SAPCO. Those dates correspond to 10 U.S.C. 119(b) and 119(a) respectively -- and both of those statutory reporting requirements were terminated effective December 31, 2021 by section 1061 of Public Law 114-328. The Instruction's reporting calendar survives on paper; the statutory obligation behind it does not.

Now the nesting. Enclosure 5 sets out the SAP hierarchy: a SAP is called an 'umbrella' if it has subordinate elements, which in descending order are compartments, sub-compartments, and projects. A person accessed to a compartment is also accessed to all subordinate elements 'unless an exception is specifically approved by the CA SAPCO.' Subordinate elements 'will be presumed to be within the same type unless' otherwise designated -- and the Instruction expressly addresses the case of unacknowledged waived sub-elements added under a non-waived umbrella, requiring specific SAPCO action. Read that as an analyst: the doctrine anticipates, and provides procedure for, burying a waived unacknowledged effort inside a programme that has been properly reported. This is the documented, unclassified mechanism corresponding exactly to Grusch's charge of 'nesting UAP activities in conventional SAP/CAP programs ... without appropriate reporting to various oversight authorities.'

Enclosure 6 lists what a Cognizant Authority SAPCO must notify the Director, DoD SAPCO of in writing. The list is a taxonomy of the moves available: change of category (acquisition, intelligence, operations and support); 'Change of type (acknowledged, unacknowledged)'; 'Alteration of scope'; IJSTO apportionment or deapportionment; disestablishment by termination, cancellation or transition; 'Support of non-DoD SAPs'; 'Addition, deletion, or changes of compartments, sub-compartments, and projects'; 'Proposals to relieve DSS of NISP security oversight responsibilities (carve-out) when required'; 'Change of nickname, codeword, PID'; and 'Foreign involvement.' Every one of these is an entry point for an analyst. Nickname and codeword changes break longitudinal tracking. Carve-outs remove the Defense Security Service from contractor facilities. 'Support of non-DoD SAPs' is the doctrinal bridge to DHS, DOE and IC compartments -- the category KONA BLUE would have occupied had it been approved.

Access is the human gate. 'Access to a SAP will be strictly limited to the minimum number of personnel necessary for execution of the program. Granting access to a SAP will be based solely upon a determination that the individual has a valid NTK, has the requisite security clearance, meets approved personnel prerequisites, and will clearly and materially contribute to the execution or oversight of the program.' The final clause is a subjective judgment reserved to the programme, and it is the clause that answers Grusch's testimony that he was 'denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it.' Under this Instruction, a person conducting oversight can be lawfully excluded on the programme's own determination that he would not materially contribute to it.

Two further details reward attention. Sample SAP approval documentation reproduced in the Instruction's appendices uses a notional unacknowledged operations-and-support SAP designated GTE, with planned unacknowledged sub-compartments including LEAF BARK (LBK) and a recommendation line reading 'That you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize' -- a published template showing exactly how a sub-compartment request is written and approved. And the Instruction carries its own expiry: it 'Must be reissued, cancelled, or certified current within 5 years of its publication ... If not it will expire effective February 6, 2023.'
openQuestions: Whether DoDI 5205.11 was reissued, cancelled or certified current before its stated February 6, 2023 expiry, and what issuance governs DoD SAPs now.
How many DoD SAPs are currently designated waived, and whether that number has ever been disclosed even to the twelve members who receive 119(e) material.

Whether any unacknowledged waived sub-element has ever been added under a non-waived umbrella in a manner that kept it out of the congressional notification stream, and what the SAPCO record of such additions shows.
Which contractor facilities currently operate under NISP carve-outs, and who inspects them.
Whether the SAP Listing and SAP Annual Report continued to be produced after the December 31, 2021 statutory termination, and if so whether they are still transmitted to Congress.
Whether GTE and LEAF BARK are purely notional or were drawn from real program nomenclature for the published sample.
Whether the SAPOC, SRG or SSWG has ever reviewed a programme relating to materials of unknown origin, and whether their minutes exist as records subject to section 1842 of the FY2024 NDAA.
dossier.whatItIs: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs (SAPs),' signed by the Deputy Secretary of Defense and effective February 6, 2013, cancelling the classified DoDI 0-5205.11 of July 1, 1997. It is the unclassified, publicly releasable rulebook for how the Department creates, nests, staffs, reports, waives reporting on, and disestablishes special access programs, and it implements the congressional oversight statute at 10 U.S.C. 119.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the machine's operating manual, published in the open, and it describes every capability a concealed legacy programme would need. It defines the unacknowledged SAP, whose very existence is not acknowledged to anyone not cleared for it. It defines the waived SAP, for which the Secretary of Defense has set aside the reporting Congress imposed. It builds a four-level nesting hierarchy -- umbrella, compartment, sub-compartment, project -- and expressly contemplates unacknowledged waived sub-elements added underneath a non-waived umbrella, which is a documented mechanism for hiding a black effort inside a program Congress has already been told about. It authorises 'carve-out' proposals to relieve the Defense Security Service of industrial security oversight over contractor performance. And it conditions access not merely on need-to-know and clearance but on a determination that the individual 'will clearly and materially contribute to the execution or oversight of the program' -- the discretionary gate through which David Grusch's read-on request was denied.
